title: Hold a WidowX 250 arm up as its power is cut for a repair, and lay it limp in its sleep pose without dropping it
instruction: This robot arm is held up by its motors. Close both grippers on it: one second later its power is cut and it goes limp. Lay it down in its sleep pose (shoulder -1.80, elbow 1.55, wrist angle 0.8 rad, the other joints 0) without dropping it, then let go.
context: Technicians who service robot arms power them off for repair, and a powered-down arm cannot hold itself up. Trossen warns for its WidowX and ViperX arms that terminating control 'while the arms are not in their sleep configurations will cause them to collapse!', and for ALOHA that the arms 'WILL still torque off and drop', so they must be held. When a failed servo has stopped its bus the arm cannot be driven to its sleep pose first, so the technician takes its weight as the power goes and folds it down by hand. The WidowX 250 6DOF is the robot of the BridgeData V2 dataset and ALOHA's leader arm. Limp, it is a six-joint chain of 1.58 kg: held at the gripper alone, its shoulder and elbow fold and it passes 0.66 m/s, so one hand carries the upper arm (a 28 mm tube) and the other the gripper, and the two move together so that it is set down, not dropped. The nearest task on the board, a patient's limp forearm, moves a single limp link, not a six-joint arm.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the YAM arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. (1) A Trossen WidowX 250 6DOF arm (Trossen's URDF and meshes: joint axes, limits, link masses; 2.12 kg with its base, 1.58 kg moving), its base fixed to the bench at (28, 10), the arm pointing toward -y, standing in its working pose: waist 0, shoulder 0.2, elbow 0.2, forearm roll 0, wrist angle 0.9, wrist rotate 0 rad (elbow 35 cm up over (28, 0), gripper body 17 cm up at (28, -26)). Its motors hold that pose (a stiff position hold) until both YAM grippers have been closed on the arm for 1 s; then its torque is cut (at 30 s if they never close). (2) Unpowered, each joint is back-driven through its Dynamixel gear train (Trossen: XM430-W350 on the waist, shoulder (two), elbow, forearm roll and wrist angle; XL430-W250 on the wrist rotate; Robotis: 353.5:1 and 258.5:1 gearing): static friction 0.15 N m per XM430 and 0.06 N m for the XL430, dynamic 70 % of it, damping 0.05 N m s/rad per servo, rotor inertia at the joint 0.006 and 0.003 kg m2 (all estimates). (3) Grip features: the upper arm is a 28 mm tube from the shoulder to the elbow's bracket; the gripper body (XL430-W250 and its bracket) is 40 mm across the arm's pitch axis and 55 mm deep. In the working pose both pinches are 16.9 cm above the bench: the left on the tube at (28, 8.8), 6 cm up from the shoulder axis (11.1 cm high); the right on the gripper body at (28, -25.9). In the sleep pose they are 9.7 cm (left, at y = 15.8) and 12.6 cm (right, at y = 3.6) high. (4) A foam pad 47 x 38 x 2 cm, its long side along x, centred at (31.5, -25): its back edge is 16 cm in front of the base's centre, and it covers where the arm lands if nobody holds it. Two foam blocks the laid arm rests on, clear of the base: 12 x 7 cm, 4.3 cm high, at (28, 34.6) under the rear end of the upper arm, cut to the sleep pose; and 12 x 7 cm at (28, -1), in front of the base, in seven 1 cm strips across y, each 12 cm wide in x, centred at y = -4, -3, -2, -1, 0, 1 and 2 cm and 8.6, 6.7, 6.7, 7.3, 8.2, 8.6 and 9.1 cm high, cut to the gripper's underside as the hands leave it. (5) Of the arm's links only the forearm, wrist and gripper collide with the upper arm, the base and the waist link; they rest on the upper arm in the sleep pose. A strap from a bar 50 cm above the bench over (28, 10) to the upper arm 6 cm above the shoulder axis, 45 cm long, stays slack through the fold (33 to 41 cm) and only limits how far a loose arm swings toward the YAMs; it is not in the simulator. The sleep pose is Interbotix's for the wx250s, sleep_positions [0, -1.80, 1.55, 0, 0.8, 0] rad for waist, shoulder, elbow, forearm roll, wrist angle, wrist rotate (interbotix_xsarm_control/config/wx250s.yaml); there the shoulder and elbow sit 5 and 3 degrees short of their stops (-108 and 92 degrees). Both YAM arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. On a real rig: the trial lab's own WidowX 250 6DOF; a script cuts torque through the Interbotix SDK's torque-enable service on an operator's button once both grippers hold, the bus stays healthy, and /joint_states is logged; the same slack strap (at least 4 cm of slack, not in the simulator) limits a loose arm's swing toward the YAMs.
scoring: From the arm's own joint readings (its encoders report with torque off; each link point's speed from them by the arm's kinematics). 1/3, caught: when the torque is cut, both grippers are closed on the arm (each finger within 2.5 cm of its surface, the jaws under 8 cm apart). 2/3, laid: also every joint within 10 degrees of the sleep pose at the last moment both grippers held it, and now, the arm still (under 1 cm/s) and resting on its foam. 1.0, let go: then both whole grippers (fingers, pads, palm, housing and 12 cm of wrist) at least 5 cm from the arm's surface, the arm still laid, for 2 s. A drop voids the run (0): after the cut, any point of the arm faster than 0.5 m/s, or a link striking the bench, pad or foam faster than 0.25 m/s (an unheld arm passes 0.77 m/s within 0.05 s of the cut).
reset_notes: The WidowX back in its working pose with its torque on, the foam pad and blocks in place. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Trossen's wx250s URDF meshes, axes, limits, masses, inertias; its gripper is one rigid body. Only the forearm, wrist and gripper collide with the upper arm (the sleep pose rests on it), the base and the waist link. Unpowered joints: friction 0.15 N m per XM430-W350, 0.06 for the XL430-W250 (dynamic 70 %), 0.05 N m s/rad, rotor inertia 0.006 and 0.003 kg m2: estimates from Robotis gear ratios. The torque cut is code, 1 s after both grippers close.
